| Field | Value |
|---|---|

| Companion package | `MARKET_DATA_CPI_U_MONTHLY_PACKAGE_2026.md` (monthly CPI-U) — required together for monthly stepping |

## 1. What this package is, and what it is not

**It is** the value-weighted total return of eligible U.S.-incorporated common stocks listed on NYSE, AMEX, and Nasdaq, at **monthly** frequency, from July 1926.

**It is not the S&P 500.** `MARKET §4.2` states this explicitly: *"This is broader than the S&P 500. Do not label it S&P 500 return."* The engine's current `HIST_RETURNS` is an S&P 500 total-return series (1928–2025, Damodaran-shaped, `MARKET §4.3`). Adopting this package is an **index change with financial meaning**, not a resolution upgrade. §7 quantifies the difference.

**It carries no inflation series.** The Fama-French library does not publish CPI. Monthly stepping additionally requires a monthly CPI-U companion (`MARKET §5.1`). That is a separate pull and is not in this package. See §12.

~~~text
This file was created using the 202607 CRSP database.
The 1-month TBill rate data until 202405 are from Ibbotson Associates. Starting from 202406, the 1-month TBill rate is from ICE BofA US 1-Month Treasury Bill Index.
The annual TBill return is compounded from the monthly T-bill rates from January to December.
~~~

| Field | `market_total_return` | `risk_free_return` |
|---|---|---|
| Frequency | Monthly | Monthly |
| Timing | Period end (calendar month) | Period end (calendar month) |
| Units in source | Percent | Percent |
| Units in package | **Decimal** | **Decimal** |
| Source columns | `Mkt-RF` + `RF` | `RF` |
| Dividend treatment | Included; reinvested on ex-date (CIZ) | n/a |
| Nominal or real | Nominal | Nominal |
| Fees | Gross of fees and taxes | n/a |

## 4. Transform specification

Per `MARKET §4.2`, applied verbatim:

~~~text
market_total_return = (Mkt_minus_RF + RF) / 100
risk_free_return    = RF / 100
~~~

Per `MARKET §10.3`, the annual series in §9 is derived by compounding, never by summing:

~~~text
annual_return[y] = product over m in 1..12 of (1 + monthly_return[y][m]) - 1
~~~

**Division by 100 is mandatory.** The source publishes percent; the engine expects decimals.

## 5. Known limitations and methodology events

1. **CIZ/FIZ methodology event.** `MARKET §4.2`: beginning with the January 2025 release the Data Library moved from CRSP FIZ to CIZ inputs. Under FIZ, monthly returns were month-to-month holding-period returns with dividends reinvested at month-end; under CIZ, monthly returns compound daily returns with dividends reinvested on ex-dates. **This package is CIZ.** Do not splice it with any pre-2025-vintage extract without a named transform and a comparison report.
2. **Historical values are not frozen.** They change when CRSP reprocesses. This is why the package carries a vintage and a hash rather than being treated as constants.
3. **Source values are published to two decimal places in percent** (1 basis point). Compounding twelve rounded monthly values introduces a small residual against the library's own published annual figures — measured at a maximum of **0.052 pp** (1980); see the invariant in §8.
4. **The risk-free series changes source mid-history.** Per the file header, 1-month T-bill data is from Ibbotson through 202405 and from the ICE BofA US 1-Month Treasury Bill Index from 202406. Treat as a second methodology event if the risk-free series is used for anything load-bearing.
5. **1926 and 2026 are partial years** (1926: 6 months; 2026: 7 months) and are excluded from the annual series in §9.

## 7. Cross-check against `HIST_RETURNS` — read this before adopting

Annual returns derived from this package (§4 formula) were compared with the engine's current `HIST_RETURNS` across the **98 overlapping complete years (1928–2025)**.

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Geometric mean, `HIST_RETURNS` (S&P 500) | **10.02%** |
| Geometric mean, this package (CRSP market) | **10.06%** |
| Difference in geometric mean | +0.04 pp |
| Mean annual difference | +0.13 pp |
| **Median absolute annual difference** | **1.85 pp** |
| **Maximum absolute annual difference** | **7.24 pp** |
| Years agreeing on sign | 94 of 98 |

**The conclusion that matters.** The two series agree on long-run compounded growth to within 4 basis points — so any test that only checks a century-long terminal wealth will not distinguish them. But they differ by a median of **1.85 percentage points in any given year**, by as much as **7.24 pp**, and they **disagree on the direction of the market in 4 years**.

Historical-replay mode walks actual year sequences, and sequence-of-returns risk is driven by individual years rather than by the long-run mean. Swapping the series will therefore move replay outcomes, failure ages, and guardrail crossings even though the long-run average is unchanged. **This is a financial model change and must be audited as one, not landed as a data refresh.**

### Years where the two series disagree on sign

| Year | `HIST_RETURNS` (S&P 500) | This package (CRSP market) |
|---|---|---|
| 1934 | -1.19% | 3.26% |
| 1939 | -1.10% | 2.51% |
| 1953 | -1.21% | 0.72% |
| 1994 | 1.33% | -0.15% |

## 8. Validation invariants

Assert these on ingestion. Each is checkable against the data in §9 and §10.

1. **Row count.** Exactly 1201 monthly observations, contiguous, no gaps, from 1926-07 to 2026-07.
2. **Month continuity.** For every consecutive pair, the later month is exactly one calendar month after the earlier.
3. **Units.** Every `market_total_return` lies in (-1, 1). A value outside that range means the divide-by-100 was skipped.
4. **Risk-free non-negativity.** Every `risk_free_return` >= 0 for this series and vintage.
5. **Compounding identity.** For each complete year, the §9 annual value equals the product of that year's twelve monthly values minus 1, to within 1e-12.
6. **Published-annual agreement.** Each derived annual value agrees with the library's own published annual row to within **0.052 pp**. A larger deviation means the parse or the transform is wrong.
7. **Vintage pinning.** The ingesting build records the archive SHA-256 from §2. A changed hash is a methodology event requiring a comparison report, never a silent refresh.

## 12. What this package still needs before an engine can use it

1. **A monthly CPI-U companion.** `MARKET §5.1` specifies CPI-U; the engine's `HIST_INFLATION` is annual. Monthly stepping needs monthly inflation aligned to the same calendar convention. Source: BLS/FRED `CPIAUCNS`, monthly from 1913. **Not included here.**
2. **A calendar-alignment decision.** `MARKET §10.2` requires recording whether each value is a month-end observation or a monthly average. This series is month-end; Shiller's price series is a monthly average. Do not join them without labelling the mismatch.
3. **An index decision, taken deliberately.** §7 shows this is not a drop-in replacement for `HIST_RETURNS`. Either adopt CRSP market and re-baseline every historical-replay fixture, or keep S&P 500 and source a monthly S&P 500 total-return series instead.
4. **A rights confirmation** before the series ships inside a distributed artifact.

---
